raw_response.country: Canada (with brief comparative overview of the United States, Australia, Greenland/Denmark, Finland, Norway, and Sweden)

criterion_notes.c1: Addresses household and community drinking water insecurity, piped vs. trucked/cistern water supply, and drinking water advisories (BWA, DNC, DNU) in First Nations reserves in Canada, although the main body focuses primarily on water quality, natural organic matter, and microbiological monitoring/treatment technologies.
criterion_notes.c2: Fails Criterion 2 under the narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type reading and is borderline/no under the plain wording. Under the plain wording, the review briefly mentions shared federal (Indigenous Services Canada, Health Canada) and First Nations administration, fragmented provincial/territorial responsibilities, and drinking water advisory classifications/guidelines as background context, but the authors explicitly state that they restricted the scope of the review to technical and microbiological issues. Under the narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type reading, it clearly fails because it does not empirically examine any rule-type mechanism governing service access (such as eligibility rules, tenure/documentation requirements, tariff/cost-recovery rules, administrative burden, or enforcement), treating governance solely as unanalysed macro-governance background while focusing on NOM removal, storage-tank biofilms, metagenomics, culturomics, and microfluidics. Even if plain Criterion 2 were treated charitably as passed based on background regulatory discussion, the full-text decision under plain Criterion 2 remains exclude due to lack of empirical evidence or systematic synthesis (Criterion 3).
criterion_notes.c3: Fails Criterion 3: this is a non-systematic narrative ('multifaceted') literature review of 169 articles and 18 government portals without systematic eligibility criteria, study selection protocol, quality assessment, or structured empirical synthesis (as confirmed by the Data Availability Statement: 'This is a literature review'). Passing reference to unpublished microbial CFU counts from two locations in one Manitoba community provides no empirical methodology or socio-legal/governance analysis.
criterion_notes.c4: Summarizes secondary government-portal counts of long-term and short-term drinking water advisories (which warn against or restrict household water consumption/use) and piped water/sanitation coverage gaps in Indigenous communities, alongside microbial and chemical water-quality indicators.
criterion_notes.c5: Fails Criterion 5: as a broad narrative technical review, there is no empirical study design linking an identifiable legal/governance exposure to a service access outcome at a defined unit of analysis.

evidence_quotes.quote: This review aims to spot the challenges and consequences of inadequate DWS and the available technical and microbiological alternatives to address water sanitation coverage in Indigenous reserves of Turtle Island.

While we restricted the scope of this review to technical and microbiological issues, we acknowledge that water insecurity is the result of socio-cultural, systemic disparities, historic and institutionalized marginalization of Indigenous people, and an ineffective and segregated system of water governance that applies to FN reserves (Meehan et al., 2020).

evidence_quotes.page: PMC PMC11493031 - Water advisories in Canada
evidence_quotes.quote: This shared administration and fragmented responsibilities has led to divergences in drinking water regulations in Indigenous reserves (Boyd, 2011; Bradford et al., 2016).

evidence_quotes.page: PMC PMC11493031 - Database search and literature screening
evidence_quotes.quote: Federal and provincial government portals were used to review the status of water advisories in Indigenous communities of Canada as well as the recommended guidelines for NOM and drinking water in the country.

Peer-reviewed publications, theses, and government portals addressing the following topics were retained for the final report: Water insecurity in Indigenous communities in Canada, DWS in Indigenous communities, Drinking water treatments, NOM, water storage tanks in Indigenous communities in Canada, microorganisms, metagenomics for water monitoring, culturomics, and microfluidics.

raw_response.exposure: not reported (scope restricted to technical water treatment methods, natural organic matter, storage container materials/biofilms, and microbiological monitoring tools rather than an empirical governance exposure)
raw_response.outcome: Secondary overview of long-term and short-term drinking water advisories, piped vs. cistern/trucked water reliance, microbial and chemical contamination risks, and performance of water treatment and molecular detection methods
raw_response.population_and_sample: Indigenous communities / First Nations reserves in Canada (narrative literature review retaining 169 scientific articles and 18 government portals)
raw_response.rationale: Excluded as E05 (No empirical evidence), as the paper is a non-systematic narrative ('multifaceted') literature review ('This is a literature review' in the Data Availability Statement) summarizing 169 articles and 18 government portals without systematic-review methodology or primary socio-legal/empirical access analysis. In addition, the authors explicitly restrict the scope of the review to technical and microbiological issues (cistern biofilms, natural organic matter removal, coagulation, biofilters, metagenomics, culturomics, and microfluidics), mentioning fragmented federal/provincial/First Nations governance only as unanalysed background rather than examining a rule-type legal or administrative mechanism governing service access (failing Criterion 2 as well).
